newsitem.title: USA: AmEx starts rewards program for investors.
newsitem.headline: AmEx starts rewards program for investors.

text.p: American Express Co said its American Express Financial Direct unit has launched a rewards program that allows investors to earn points that can be redeemed for airline travel, hotel accomodations, car rentals, golf instructions and retail purchases.
A spokeswoman said the program was more comprehensive than those offered by competitors.

Customers will earn one point for every $10.00 invested through Financial Direct. American Express said the deposits can be used to invest in more than 200 no-load mutual funds, money market accounts, brokerage services and InvestDirect, the new online investing service.
American Express said in an introductory offer investors can earn double points or one point for every $5.00 deposited before December 31, 1996.

Points are earned on deposits of $5,000 or more and are tabulated based on net new deposits. Deposits must be held for a minimum of 90 days to earn points, with January 31, 1997 being the earliest redemption date. American Express said points will be granted on that date to all current financial direct customers with investments of more than $5,000. Participation in the program is free and qualifying customers are automatically enrolled, the company said.
The company said its American Express Financial Advisors unit plans to add a rewards program tied to financial planning in early 1997.
The company said it has more than 40 partners for the program including 12 airlines, three car rental companies, nine gourmet shops and 14 retailers.
Corporate and institutional accounts are not eligible for points, the company said.
